hypothesis.count_consequence: Count-ASYMMETRIC by construction and unavoidably so: the cure must ADD two instructions (the stfd/lfd pair) and 8 bytes of frame, taking ours from 102 to 104 and 128 to 136. That is why no postprocessor class can serve this function and why every probe must be read on the multiset delta rather than on real.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- every offset, register and instruction above is read from the target's own `fnasm` dump and from our compiled object at c8a28c3bb, and the 1:1 instruction correspondence was checked against the multiset delta rather than assumed. hypothesis.statement: The residual is a SCHEDULE difference wearing a register-allocation costume, and the carrier is ONE load: the target hoists `@0x130 lfs f6,60(r9)` (viewport->yoff) 0x34 bytes ahead of its consumer `@0x164 fadd f2,f6,f2`, while our object loads the same value at `@0x158`, 0x8 ahead of its consumer at `@0x160`. The target's x half does the SAME hoist -- `@0xd0 lfs f3,56(r9)` (viewport->xoff) 0x38 ahead of `@0x108 fadd f2,f3,f0` -- and OUR x half already matches it at `@0xcc` -> `@0x100`, 0x34. So the two halves are SYMMETRIC in the target and ASYMMETRIC in ours, and the y-half load is the single live range we are not carrying. The next lane should aim at the SCHEDULE of that one load with the local block held byte-for-byte constant (adding or removing a declaration is now measured dead in both directions), and should read the result on the multiset delta, never on real.
